_about: Planedex catalog: every aircraft type that could realistically fly within range of Spokane. Species are ICAO aircraft type codes, plus a few military variants the push script derives (VC25, KC46, C32, C40, C37, C21, C12). types: jet, regional, heavy, jumbo, bizjet, turboprop, prop, rotor, military, fire, oddball. rarity: 1 Common, 2 Uncommon, 3 Rare, 4 Epic, 5 Legendary. A type code the receiver catches that isn't listed here still counts; planedex_push.py prints it so it can be added (then run fetch_photos.py for its photo).

A319.name: Airbus A319
A319.fact: A shorter A320, built for smaller routes.

A320.name: Airbus A320
A320.fact: The first airliner with digital fly-by-wire controls.

A20N.name: Airbus A320neo

A321.name: Airbus A321

A339.name: Airbus A330-900

A124.name: Antonov An-124 Ruslan

GLEX.name: Bombardier Global Express / 6000

GLF6.name: Gulfstream G650
GLF6.fact: One of the fastest business jets in the sky.

SF50.name: Cirrus Vision Jet

PC24.name: Pilatus PC-24

PC12.name: Pilatus PC-12

BE20.name: Beechcraft King Air 200

MU2.name: Mitsubishi MU-2

P46T.name: Piper M500

T206.name: Cessna Turbo Stationair

P28R.name: Piper Arrow
P28R.fact: A four-seat Piper whose landing gear folds up.

BE19.name: Beechcraft Sport

AEST.name: Aerostar 600

SR22.name: Cirrus SR22

B407.name: Bell 407

EC35.name: Airbus H135

R22.name: Robinson R22

R44.name: Robinson R44
R44.fact: A four-seat helicopter, the R22's bigger sibling.

B212.name: Bell UH-1N Iroquois
B212.fact: The twin-engine version of the famous Huey helicopter.

C17.name: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III

VC25.name: Boeing VC-25A / E-4B

CL2T.name: Canadair CL-415 Super Scooper

AT8T.name: Air Tractor AT-802

B762.name: Boeing 767-200

C180.name: Cessna 180 Skywagon

COL4.name: Cessna 400 Corvalis

F2TH.name: Dassault Falcon 2000

A19N.name: Airbus A319neo

CRJ2.name: Bombardier CRJ200

CRJX.name: Bombardier CRJ1000

CL30.name: Bombardier Challenger 300

GL5T.name: Bombardier Global 5000

LJ60.name: Learjet 60

C82R.name: Cessna Skylane RG
C82R.fact: A Skylane with wheels that fold up in flight.

C195.name: Cessna 195
C195.fact: A 1940s Cessna with a big round radial engine.

LA4.name: Lake Buccaneer
LA4.fact: An amphibian with its engine perched high above the wing.

NAVI.name: Navion
NAVI.fact: A 1940s four-seater designed by the makers of the P-51 Mustang.

ST75.name: Boeing Stearman
ST75.fact: A bright biplane trainer from World War II.

PTS1.name: Pitts S-1 Special
PTS1.fact: A one-seat biplane so small it fits in a garage.

PTS2.name: Pitts S-2 Special
PTS2.fact: A tiny two-seat biplane built for airshow stunts.

E300.name: Extra 300
E300.fact: A German stunt plane built for aerobatic contests and airshows.

YK52.name: Yak-52
YK52.fact: A Russian-designed aerobatic trainer with a radial engine.

C310.name: Cessna 310
C310.fact: A sleek twin. One starred in the old TV show 'Sky King'.

C402.name: Cessna 402
C402.fact: A small twin flown by commuter airlines.

C414.name: Cessna Chancellor
C414.fact: A pressurized twin built to fly above the weather.

C421.name: Cessna Golden Eagle
C421.fact: Cessna's biggest piston twin, with a pressurized cabin.

C337.name: Cessna Skymaster
C337.fact: Push-pull! One propeller in front and one in back.

PA31.name: Piper Navajo
PA31.fact: A cabin-class twin used for charters and cargo.

PA34.name: Piper Seneca
PA34.fact: A twin-engine Piper that many pilots train in.

PA44.name: Piper Seminole
PA44.fact: A twin-engine trainer with a T-tail.

BE58.name: Beechcraft Baron 58
BE58.fact: A bigger Baron with six seats.

AC50.name: Aero Commander 500
AC50.fact: A high-wing twin. Famous pilot Bob Hoover flew one in airshows.

DA42.name: Diamond DA42 Twin Star
DA42.fact: A twin that burns jet fuel instead of gasoline.

DA62.name: Diamond DA62
DA62.fact: A seven-seat diesel twin from Austria.

P51.name: P-51 Mustang
P51.fact: A famous World War II fighter. Only about 150 still fly.

B17.name: B-17 Flying Fortress
B17.fact: A four-engine World War II bomber. Only a handful still fly.

B25.name: B-25 Mitchell
B25.fact: A twin-engine World War II bomber. A few still visit airshows.

CORS.name: F4U Corsair
CORS.fact: A World War II fighter with bent 'gull' wings.

SPIT.name: Supermarine Spitfire
SPIT.fact: The famous British fighter from World War II.

L39.name: Aero L-39 Albatros
L39.fact: A Czech jet trainer that some people own and fly for fun.

C30J.name: C-130J Super Hercules
C30J.fact: A modern Hercules with six-blade propellers.

E3TF.name: E-3 Sentry
E3TF.fact: The AWACS: a jet with a giant spinning radar dish on its back.

E6.name: E-6 Mercury
E6.fact: A Navy jet that can talk to submarines by trailing a wire miles long.

R135.name: RC-135
R135.fact: A spy plane based on the KC-135, with a bulging 'hog nose'.

P3.name: P-3 Orion
P3.fact: A four-engine sub hunter. NOAA flies two as Hurricane Hunters.

B1.name: B-1B Lancer
B1.fact: A bomber whose wings swing back so it can fly faster than sound.

B2.name: B-2 Spirit
B2.fact: A flying-wing stealth bomber. Only about 20 were ever built.

F15.name: F-15 Eagle
F15.fact: A twin-engine fighter that can fly more than twice the speed of sound.

F16.name: F-16 Fighting Falcon
F16.fact: A nimble fighter that pilots call the 'Viper'.

F18H.name: F/A-18 Hornet
F18H.fact: The Navy and Marine fighter the Blue Angels flew for decades.

F18S.name: F/A-18 Super Hornet
F18S.fact: A bigger Hornet. The Growlers based on Whidbey Island are built from it.

F35.name: F-35 Lightning II
F35.fact: A stealth fighter designed to hide from radar.

F22.name: F-22 Raptor
F22.fact: A stealth fighter that can cruise faster than sound without afterburners.

A10.name: A-10 Thunderbolt II
A10.fact: The 'Warthog', built around a huge cannon.

T38.name: T-38 Talon
T38.fact: A supersonic trainer. NASA astronauts fly them too.

TEX2.name: T-6 Texan II
TEX2.fact: The first plane new Air Force and Navy pilots learn to fly.

E2.name: E-2 Hawkeye
E2.fact: A Navy radar plane with a big round dish that lands on aircraft carriers.

Q4.name: RQ-4 Global Hawk
Q4.fact: A giant drone with no pilot aboard that can stay up for more than a day.

U2.name: Lockheed U-2
U2.fact: A spy plane that flies above 70,000 feet, at the edge of space.

C32.name: Boeing C-32
C32.fact: A military 757. When the Vice President is aboard, it becomes Air Force Two.

C40.name: Boeing C-40 Clipper
C40.fact: A military 737 that carries VIPs and cargo.

C37.name: Gulfstream C-37
C37.fact: A military Gulfstream that flies generals and government officials.

C21.name: Learjet C-21
C21.fact: A military Learjet that flies people and urgent cargo.

C12.name: Beechcraft C-12 Huron
C12.fact: A military King Air flown by every branch of the armed forces.

H60.name: UH-60 Black Hawk
H60.fact: A tough Army helicopter. Firefighting versions are called Firehawks.

H47.name: CH-47 Chinook
H47.fact: A big helicopter with two giant rotors.

H64.name: AH-64 Apache
H64.fact: An Army attack helicopter with a sensor pod on its nose.

B06.name: Bell 206 JetRanger
B06.fact: One of the most popular helicopters ever built.

B412.name: Bell 412
B412.fact: A tough twin-engine helicopter with four blades.

B429.name: Bell 429
B429.fact: A modern twin-engine helicopter often used as an air ambulance.

B505.name: Bell 505 Jet Ranger X
B505.fact: The newest little Bell, with a big glass cockpit.

UH1.name: Bell UH-1 Huey
UH1.fact: The famous 'Huey'. Some old Hueys now fight fires.

B47G.name: Bell 47
B47G.fact: A bubble-canopy helicopter from the 1940s and 1950s.

AS50.name: Airbus H125
AS50.fact: One of these once landed on top of Mount Everest!

AS55.name: Airbus AS355 Twin Squirrel
AS55.fact: A twin-engine version of the H125.

EC20.name: Airbus EC120
EC20.fact: A small, quiet helicopter with a fan hidden in its tail.

EC30.name: Airbus H130
EC30.fact: A tour helicopter with a wide cabin and a fan in its tail.

EC45.name: Airbus H145
EC45.fact: A twin-engine helicopter flown by air ambulances and police.

H500.name: MD 500
H500.fact: A small egg-shaped helicopter, famous from TV and movies.

MD52.name: MD 520N
MD52.fact: A helicopter with no tail rotor. It steers with air blowing out of its tail.

S76.name: Sikorsky S-76
S76.fact: A sleek twin-engine helicopter used by air ambulances and companies.

S92.name: Sikorsky S-92
S92.fact: A big helicopter. A version of it flies the President as Marine One.

A119.name: AgustaWestland AW119 Koala
A119.fact: A single-engine helicopter built in Philadelphia.

A139.name: AgustaWestland AW139
A139.fact: A big twin used for search and rescue.

KMAX.name: Kaman K-MAX
KMAX.fact: A one-seat helicopter whose two rotors mesh like an eggbeater, built to lift heavy loads.

S64.name: Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane
S64.fact: It can suck up more than 2,500 gallons of water to drop on wildfires.

S61.name: Sikorsky S-61
S61.fact: A big 1960s helicopter. Some now fight fires or haul logs.

EN28.name: Enstrom F-28
EN28.fact: A small piston helicopter built in Michigan.

EN48.name: Enstrom 480
EN48.fact: A turbine Enstrom with a roomy cabin.

H269.name: Schweizer 300
H269.fact: A little helicopter used for training and spraying crops.

B462.name: BAe 146-200
B462.fact: A small four-engine jet. Neptune Aviation in Missoula flies them as air tankers.

RJ85.name: Avro RJ85
RJ85.fact: A four-engine regional jet now used to drop fire retardant.

GLID.name: Glider
GLID.fact: No engine at all. It rides rising columns of warm air.

BALL.name: Hot air balloon
BALL.fact: It floats on heated air. Most balloons don't broadcast, so this is a rare catch.

GYRO.name: Gyroplane
GYRO.fact: Its rotor spins freely in the wind while a propeller pushes it along.

SHIP.name: Airship
SHIP.fact: A blimp! It floats on helium.

CH7B.name: Citabria
CH7B.fact: Its name is 'airbatic' spelled backward. It's built for loops and rolls.

C82S.name: Cessna Turbo Skylane
C82S.fact: A Skylane with a turbocharger that pumps extra air into the engine, so it stays strong up high.

K900.name: Kodiak 900
K900.fact: The bigger, faster cousin of the Kodiak 100, also built in Sandpoint, Idaho.

C82T.name: Cessna Turbo Skylane RG
C82T.fact: A turbo Skylane whose wheels tuck up into the plane in flight, so it slips through the air faster.

C188.name: Cessna AgTruck
C188.fact: A tough one-seat Cessna made for spraying crops, with a big tank right in front of the pilot.

P337.name: Cessna Pressurized Skymaster
P337.fact: One engine pulls in front and one pushes in back. This one has a pressurized cabin for flying high.

O1.name: Cessna O-1 Bird Dog
O1.fact: A little 1950s Army scout plane built to fly low and slow and spot things from above.

C162.name: Cessna Skycatcher
C162.fact: Cessna's little light-sport trainer. Only a few hundred were built.

C501.name: Cessna Citation I/SP
C501.fact: A Citation I set up to be flown by just one pilot. That is what the SP stands for.

COL3.name: Cessna 350 Corvalis
COL3.fact: A sleek all-composite plane that began life as the Columbia 350, built in Bend, Oregon.

PA11.name: Piper Cub Special
PA11.fact: A late-1940s Cub with its engine fully covered, so the cylinders don't stick out like on the J-3.

J5.name: Piper Cub Cruiser
J5.fact: A wider 1940s Cub with the pilot up front and room for two passengers behind.

PA20.name: Piper Pacer
PA20.fact: A stubby 1950s four-seat taildragger. Its tricycle-gear twin is the Tri-Pacer.

PA38.name: Piper Tomahawk
PA38.fact: A 1970s two-seat trainer with a T-shaped tail and big windows all around.

BE30.name: Beechcraft King Air 300
BE30.fact: A more powerful King Air from the 1980s. The King Air 350 grew out of it.

BE10.name: Beechcraft King Air 100
BE10.fact: A stretched King Air with room for more passengers, first built in 1969.

BT36.name: Beechcraft Turbo Bonanza
BT36.fact: A six-seat Bonanza with a turbocharger to stay strong high over the mountains.

BE60.name: Beechcraft Duke
BE60.fact: A sleek 1970s twin with turbocharged engines and a pressurized cabin.

T34P.name: Beechcraft T-34 Mentor
T34P.fact: A 1950s military trainer built from the Bonanza. Many now fly with private owners.

TAYB.name: Taylorcraft
TAYB.fact: A 1930s two-seater where pilot and passenger sit side by side, unlike the Cub.

AR11.name: Aeronca Chief
AR11.fact: A friendly 1940s side-by-side two-seater, a cousin of the Aeronca Champ.

GC1.name: Globe Swift
GC1.fact: A zippy 1940s two-seater with a sliding canopy and wheels that fold up.

B14A.name: Bellanca Cruisair
B14A.fact: A 1940s four-seater with wooden wings and three tail fins.

FA24.name: Fairchild Argus
FA24.fact: A 1930s cabin plane that also served in World War II as a light transport.

WACF.name: Waco biplane
WACF.fact: A 1930s open-cockpit biplane from Waco, one of the biggest plane makers of its day.

G164.name: Grumman Ag-Cat
G164.fact: A big biplane built just for spraying crops, first flown in 1957.

AT5T.name: Air Tractor AT-504
AT5T.fact: A two-seat Air Tractor used to train new crop-spraying pilots.

AT3T.name: Air Tractor AT-402
AT3T.fact: A turboprop crop sprayer from Air Tractor in Olney, Texas.

SS2T.name: Turbo Thrush
SS2T.fact: A turboprop crop duster with a tank that holds hundreds of gallons of spray.

SS2P.name: Thrush Commander
SS2P.fact: The piston-engine Thrush crop duster, from a design that dates back to the 1950s.

GLAS.name: Glasair
GLAS.fact: A speedy kit plane that people build in their garages. Glasair started in Washington state.

GLST.name: GlaStar
GLST.fact: A high-wing kit plane from Glasair in Arlington, Washington. It can fly on wheels or floats.

LGEZ.name: Rutan Long-EZ
LGEZ.fact: A homebuilt with a little wing up front and its engine in back, pushing.

VEZE.name: Rutan VariEze
VEZE.fact: Burt Rutan's 1970s homebuilt with the wing in front. It looks like it's flying backward.

LNC2.name: Lancair 320
LNC2.fact: A tiny, very fast two-seat kit plane first designed in Oregon.

VELO.name: Velocity
VELO.fact: A four-seat kit plane with a little wing up front and a pusher engine in back.

LNP4.name: Lancair Propjet
LNP4.fact: A turbine-powered version of the speedy Lancair IV kit plane.

FDCT.name: Flight Design CT
FDCT.fact: A German light-sport two-seater made from carbon-fiber composites.

CRUZ.name: SportCruiser
CRUZ.fact: A Czech light-sport two-seater. Piper once sold it as the PiperSport.

CH60.name: Zenith Zodiac
CH60.fact: A two-seat kit plane with a big bubble canopy, often built at home.

CH70.name: Zenith STOL CH 701
CH70.fact: A boxy kit plane made to take off and land in really short spaces.

CH75.name: Zenith Cruzer
CH75.fact: A roomy, easygoing kit plane, the cruising cousin of Zenith's short-field STOL 750.

SONX.name: Sonex
SONX.fact: A small, simple kit plane designed to be affordable to build and fun to fly.

WAIX.name: Sonex Waiex
WAIX.fact: A Sonex with a Y-shaped tail instead of a regular one.

M5.name: Maule M-5
M5.fact: A tough four-seat taildragger built for short, rough backcountry strips.

CC19.name: CubCrafters XCub
CC19.fact: A modern super-Cub built by CubCrafters in Yakima, Washington.

SREY.name: SeaRey
SREY.fact: A little two-seat kit plane that's also a boat, so it can take off from water.

BL17.name: Bellanca Viking
BL17.fact: A fast four-seater with wooden wings, a rare thing in modern planes.

EXEC.name: RotorWay Exec
EXEC.fact: A two-seat helicopter that people build themselves from a kit.

UH12.name: Hiller UH-12
UH12.fact: A bubble-cockpit helicopter first flown in 1948.

EAGL.name: Christen Eagle
EAGL.fact: A colorful aerobatic biplane built from a kit, famous for its bright sunburst paint.

GLIM.name: Motor glider
GLIM.fact: A glider with a small engine. It can take off on its own, then shut the engine off and soar.

CJ6.name: Nanchang CJ-6
CJ6.fact: A Chinese military trainer from the late 1950s. Many now fly with private owners.
